A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and clearly describe successive versions of the same Gaussian-based occupancy work. V1 includes Supplementary Material A-D, whereas v2 ends at the references despite citing supplementary material in Section 4.5. This limits comparison of supporting analyses and implementation details.

before.justification: V1 reports original OccGS benchmark results, component ablations, initialization experiments, threshold sensitivity, and qualitative failure cases in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: V2 reports original AutoOcc-V and AutoOcc-M results on Occ3D-nuScenes and SemanticKITTI, annotation-efficiency measurements, and component ablations.

M1.justification: V1's Grounding-DINO/SAM pipeline driven by supplied semantic prompts becomes a dynamically generated category list with semantic attention, category merging, attention-guided segmentation, and learned-depth pseudo-points in v2. Motion correspondence is also reformulated. These substantially change the procedure beyond renaming SGAG as VL-GS, although cumulative Gaussian-to-voxel splatting is retained. V1's appendix already tested a vision-only SfM variant.

E1.justification: Reported coverage remains Occ3D-nuScenes and cross-dataset SemanticKITTI, including the same displayed base and novel semantic classes. Dynamic objects, rain, nighttime, and vision-only inputs already appear in v1, including its appendix. The annotation framing and new model variants do not establish a separate evaluated task or new dataset coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 2 replaces v1's broad prediction comparison with annotation-oriented comparators, adding OpenOcc*, OVIR-3D, and VLM-LiDAR while retaining GaussianOcc, LangOcc, and VEON. SurroundOcc changes from a supervised predictor to an annotation-pipeline comparison using VLM-derived semantics. The SemanticKITTI comparison also replaces TPVFormer, GaussianFormer, and OccNeRF with SurroundOcc and VLM-LiDAR.

E3.justification: V2 explicitly extends self-supervised comparators with historical-frame aggregation and global temporal fusion, and substitutes VLM semantics for manual priors in annotation pipelines. Generated categories are mapped to benchmark labels using CLIP. Efficiency evaluation changes from inference latency and per-scene training time to annotation hours and representation counts. The stated image-resolution and AdamW schedules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The main-text scaling ablation changes from disabling foreground/background decoupling in v1 Table 4 to replacing SSG with vanilla Gaussians in v2 Table 5. Dynamics and geometry-loss tests persist, and the dynamic qualitative example is reused. However, v1's initialization, threshold-sensitivity, semantic-prior, and failure-case analyses cannot be matched against v2's unavailable supplement, leaving the full extent of change uncertain.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The available tables retain single-point reporting; changes in reported scores do not constitute a change in uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V1 reports OccGS-Z at 83.82 IoU/30.26 mIoU on nuScenes and 49.98/15.97 on SemanticKITTI; v2 reports AutoOcc-M at 88.62/25.84 and 41.23/12.76, respectively. V2 adds AutoOcc-V and new comparator results and replaces efficiency measurements. OVO's reported SemanticKITTI mIoU changes from 6.94 to 5.83. Revised methods and protocols prevent interpreting these as performance changes under fixed conditions.

T1.justification: V2 introduces an attention-aggregation definition and a Chamfer-distance correspondence objective, and revises the motion indicator from v1's double-sum cluster expression to a paired-Gaussian single sum. The Gaussian density, semantic blending, geometry loss, and cumulative splatting equations remain essentially unchanged. Neither version provides theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes zero-shot, open-vocabulary occupancy reconstruction and competitiveness with supervised predictors. V2 redefines the central contribution as automatic open-ended occupancy annotation without predefined category lists, emphasizing vision-centric operation and superiority over annotation pipelines. Label-free reconstruction and cross-dataset generalization remain shared claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations linking attention-guided category integration to reduced ambiguity and identifies learned-depth errors as a source of geometric distortion. Interpretations concerning temporal consistency and adverse-weather reconstruction largely persist. Whether v1's explicit residual-VLM-error limitation in Appendix D survives in the later supplement cannot be established.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies CogVLM-17B, EVA2-CLIP-E, Vicuna-7B-v1.5, and CLIP category mapping, and promises future code/model release without supplying access. Core optimization schedules match v1. V1 also documents eight A100 GPUs, rho=4, keyframe-only training, and opacity pruning; their retention in v2's unavailable supplement cannot be checked, preventing a reliable assessment of the full reproducibility change.

R1.justification: The research positioning shifts from competing primarily with occupancy predictors to competing with automatic annotation pipelines. V2 adds dedicated annotation and open-world-understanding discussions, distinguishes open-set from open-ended recognition, and incorporates works such as GenerateU, attention-as-prompts, OVIR-3D, and UniDepth. This substantially revises the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: Beyond the OccGS-to-AutoOcc renaming, the abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. The method is reorganized around Vision-Language Guidance and VL-GS, the standalone dataset section disappears, and comparisons are regrouped around annotation-pipeline types rather than supervision levels.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 are substantially redrawn, and v2 adds a scalable-Gaussian illustration and an annotation-pipeline comparison table. Performance tables replace supervision columns with input modalities, and the efficiency table has a different structure. Qualitative comparisons are recomposed with new comparator and modality rows; v2 Figure 6 reuses v1 Figure 5 rather than adding a new case.

improvement.justification: V2 explains automatic category discovery more explicitly and aligns comparisons more closely with annotation, including temporal adaptation of self-supervised baselines. However, its expanded open-ended claim is evaluated through mapping generated labels back to the same benchmark categories, and the missing referenced supplement prevents checking whether v1's diagnostics, failure discussion, and implementation details remain available. These gains and unresolved evidence gaps prevent a reliable net quality judgment; the revised performance numbers alone do not establish improvement.
